findings.title: VIEW permission is treated as MANAGE for groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). The global canManage() check is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() through requireManage(), so a caller with only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is allowed to create top-level groups. This is a privilege escalation; the method should require only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.

findings.title: Group view-permission lookup returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates group resources but adds groupResource.getId() to the result and passes that same resource ID into hasPermission(). Callers expect actual group IDs: UsersResource.getUsersCount(realm, ..., getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()) and UsersResource.searchForUser() storing the set under UserModel.GROUPS both use the result as a group-ID filter. Because group resources are named by group ID (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup() returns group.getId()), this produces a set containing resource IDs that match no group, so user search/count filters can return no users or wrong results. It also means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are not evaluated, because findByName(server, resourceId) fails and falls back to the all-groups resource. Use the group ID/name from the resource and evaluate that.

findings.title: Per-type resources are created without their resource type
findings.body: In getOrCreateResource(), resources created for the schema resource types (now including Groups) are persisted with resourceStore.create(...) but resource.setType(resourceType) is never called. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers group resources via resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). Group resources created when a group-specific permission is added will therefore have no type and will be skipped by that lookup, so group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are ignored by the group filtering path. Set the resource type when creating the resource.

findings.title: Created test group is not cleaned up
findings.body: testManageAllGroups() creates a group named "testGroup" through realmAdminClient but never registers it in realm.cleanup(), unlike the other groups created in this test class. Other tests assume exact group counts (for example testViewGroups() expects exactly two visible groups after granting view-all), so this leftover group can make the suite order-dependent and flaky. Register the group for cleanup or remove it at the end of the test.
